0 the generator
1 a signed value narrower than 64 bits is extended with zeros
2 unsigned values are compared as signed
3 an array or slice index is not checked against the length
4 a field read through a pointer takes the offset of the field before it
5 arguments 1 and 2 travel in each other's register
6 an add that leaves its type does not trap
7 a zero divisor does not trap
8 every shift count is masked with 63
9 a cast of a signed value to a wider type fills with zeros
10 a stack argument is read one slot too high
11 a subtract that leaves its type does not trap
12 a multiply that leaves its type does not trap
13 an indexed store writes eight bytes whatever the element width
14 a signed remainder is taken as unsigned
15 an aggregate result is copied back for its first 8 bytes only
16 a hex number is padded with spaces where the format asks for zeros
17 a negative decimal number is printed with no minus sign
18 less-or-equal is compiled as less-than
19 a vector index is not checked against the length
20 a wrapping subtract takes its operands the wrong way round
21 the smallest signed value divided by -1 does not trap
22 a right shift of a signed value fills with zeros
